title: Stereotypical Bias Removal for Hate Speech Detection Task using Knowledge-based Generalizations
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured stereotypical bias in hate speech detection models, specifically focusing on how models incorrectly associate identity terms with hateful content. This included measuring bias against a curated list of religious identity words (e.g., muslim, christian, jewish, sikh) by evaluating the model's prediction probabilities on text containing these words.
findings: The study found that hate speech detection models can develop stereotypical biases, incorrectly flagging content containing religious identity terms (e.g., 'muslim', 'sikh', 'jewish') as hateful. The authors demonstrated that their proposed knowledge-based generalization techniques—such as replacing specific religious terms with more general hypernyms (e.g., 'sikh' with 'disciple')—effectively reduced this bias. This mitigation was achieved without a significant loss in the overall accuracy of the hate speech detection task.
